rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify limiting pairs while aiming to elute all 10 compounds near 10 minutes. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the crowded central pairs respond to slope. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, allowing more separation without a substantial time penalty.

The limiting pair improved substantially with a shallower gradient, so reduce the slope further. Raising the starting organic fraction should offset much of the added retention time while keeping the first peak retained, targeting full resolution before 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to bring the last peak below 10 minutes. The slightly shallower gradient should preserve the limiting pair’s full resolution, while the early peaks have ample separation.

Injection 4 already achieved the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a 5 °C increase to shorten retention and determine whether temperature improves the limiting pair’s resolution margin while retaining CRF 1.000.

Retain injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a faster, high-temperature method. The strong temperature response suggests the limiting pair may separate again after an elution-order reversal; this run tests that possibility with a shorter gradient.

Lower temperature one step to open the new limiting pair seen at 60 °C, while testing whether the other central pair remains resolved. This could retain the maximum CRF with a substantially shorter elution time than injection 4.

The limiting central pair appears to reverse order between 55 and 60 °C. Test a steeper gradient at 60 °C to see whether slope shifts it farther apart while shortening elution; injection 4 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Test a higher starting organic fraction to shift the selectivity of the unresolved central pair at 60 °C. Use a 10-minute gradient to protect neighboring separations, while checking that the early peaks remain sufficiently retained and resolved.

Test an intermediate temperature with the shorter gradient to seek full resolution after the central pair’s apparent order reversal, without the new overlap seen at 55–60 °C. Injection 4 remains the maximum-score benchmark; this run explores a faster alternative.

Lower the starting organic fraction relative to injection 7 to test whether the limiting central pair opens while preserving the other close pair. This also improves early-peak retention and should keep the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Lengthen only the gradient from injection 11 to improve the remaining R = 1.29 pair and check that the R = 1.61 pair stays resolved. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially matching the maximum score with faster elution than injection 4.

Use a slope between injections 11 and 12 by narrowing the organic window and shortening the programmed gradient. This should retain full resolution while eluting the last peak slightly earlier than injection 12 and well before the final hold.

Slightly steepen the gradient relative to injection 13 to shorten elution while targeting resolution just above 1.5 for both limiting pairs. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so all compounds should elute during the gradient.

With the maximum CRF secured, explore lower-temperature selectivity for a potentially faster fully resolved method. A 10-minute broad gradient should keep the last peak near the unpenalized window while testing whether the central overlaps separate at 30 °C.

Return to the successful 55 °C region and lower the starting organic fraction to improve central-pair selectivity. The steeper slope than injection 14 may shorten last-peak retention while the lower starting fraction compensates for the limiting pair’s loss of resolution.

Preserve injection 16’s successful gradient slope exactly while ending the ramp at 0.65 organic. Since the last peak eluted at 7.60 minutes, before this shortened gradient reaches the outlet at 8.65 minutes, the separation should retain CRF 1.000.

Increase the gradient slope slightly from 0.075 to 0.080 organic fraction per minute to test whether elution can be shortened further without losing full resolution. The limiting pairs have little margin, so retain injection 17 as the proven maximum-score method if this steeper gradient compromises separation.

Seek a larger resolution margin at the maximum CRF rather than further compressing the narrowly resolved method. Relative to injection 7, the shallower gradient should improve the limiting pair substantially, with the last peak projected to remain below 10 minutes.

Slightly steepen injection 19’s gradient to shorten elution while retaining its improved selectivity. Interpolation from the 12- and 18-minute gradients suggests both limiting pairs can remain above R = 1.5, preserving the maximum CRF.

Explore a second maximum-score operating region near injection 4 by combining a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. This may improve the central-pair resolution margin while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes; the early pair’s separation will also be checked.

Trim injection 19’s gradient window while keeping nearly the same slope, targeting its larger resolution margin with a shorter programmed ramp. The estimated last-peak elution fraction is about 0.54, so a final fraction of 0.60 should keep all peaks within the gradient and preserve CRF 1.000.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 12 to increase the central R = 1.77 separation while checking that the less slope-responsive R = 1.57 pair retains full resolution. This should provide another maximum-score method with the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 19 to improve its limiting central separation while checking that the other close pair remains resolved. The last peak is projected near 9.8 minutes, potentially preserving CRF 1.000 with a larger resolution margin.

Use a slope between injections 19 and 24, targeting balanced limiting-pair resolutions near 1.7 and last-peak elution around 9.5 minutes. This final refinement should preserve the already-achieved maximum CRF of 1.000 with more resolution margin than the fastest successful method.
